clone_cost.note: our estimate with assumptions visible; not a claim about the team

assumptions: you pick one jurisdiction and one industry first, because 16 rulesets is a company not a hackathon
you have a GCP project you can run Cloud Tasks, BigQuery and Workflows against, and IAM rights to deny yourself
a domain reviewer is available; without one the rulesets are your own guess about the law
value.estimate: 2-3 weeks for the agent pair, gateway and append-only trail; months for defensible rulesets
value.why: The infrastructure they describe is standard GCP work and their two structural tricks are small to implement once you know them. What cannot be hurried is authoring and maintaining rule text for the jurisdictions you serve, plus someone qualified to confirm each rule still matches the regulation.

data_and_models.value: No model training. Two Gemini calls - fact extraction, then reasoning against hand-written versioned YAML rulesets - with citation mandatory in the output schema and prompt plus model version recorded per check. The regulated content is the rulesets themselves, authored by the team; nothing on the page says who reviewed them against the current text of the regulations they cite.

how_it_works.value: Five containerised services on Cloud Run behind one FastAPI gateway, declared in Terraform, running in a real GCP project with no emulators. Ingestion and compliance agents are Cloud Tasks workers (OIDC between them); state lives in Firestore, the audit trail in append-only BigQuery, documents and reports in Cloud Storage; a Cloud Scheduler job triggers Cloud Workflows for the weekly report. React dashboard with Firebase Auth on the front. Two decisions carry the design: tenant identity is taken only from verified JWT claims, never from a body or query parameter, so no code path can read across tenants; and rewriting an audit row needs both bigquery.tables.updateData and bigquery.jobs.create, so the writer identity holds the first and is denied the second - UPDATE and DELETE are unavailable to their own application rather than merely unused by it.

how_they_tested.value: Pytest is declared in Built With and 536 tests are reported, including a named concurrency case, but no repository, CI run or test output is linked, so the count and the coverage are the team's assertion. No accuracy figure is claimed for the compliance verdicts themselves - no eval set of documents with known-correct outcomes, no false-positive or missed-finding rate against an auditor's judgement.

limits_they_disclosed.value: Prompting does not stop fabrication, so rules live in versioned YAML, a citation is mandatory in the output contract, prompt and model version are recorded against every check so a verdict can be reproduced, and when the model cannot ground a verdict it escalates instead of guessing. Their weekly report workflow existed, was scheduled and looked healthy in the console for three weeks without ever running: Cloud Scheduler was being refused with PERMISSION_DENIED into a log nobody read, and fixing it uncovered six defects behind each other (missing invoker role, doubled URL scheme, a request to a route the service does not serve, a hardcoded tenant list, a service account without Firestore access, a missing log-writer permission). They conclude the actual bug was that nothing was watching; there are now uptime checks and alerts on scheduler and workflow failures. Terraform silently dropped a hand-set environment variable because Cloud Run replaces its env list wholesale, which cost every platform admin console access at once; the same trap sat in payment flags where a default of false would have quietly removed PayPal credentials on a fresh checkout, so those variables are now required and a missing value stops the deploy. An unregistered domestic Razorpay account rejects international cards even in live mode, and Stripe's INR conversion fee turned a $50 audit into a much larger rupee figure at checkout, so they removed Stripe and use PayPal for international customers.

value.relation: same audience, opposite instrument: that project signs an execution claim so a verifier can reject a mutation, this one cites a rule so a human can reject a reading. Read together they cover both halves of machine-checkable compliance - provenance and interpretation.

same shape (an agent pipeline that hands edge cases to a human) with a different optimisation target: Greenlight spends less, ComplianceGuardian refuses to be wrong quietly. The escalation path is the shared skeleton worth copying from either.

what_breaks_first.value: The rulesets. Eighty-eight hand-authored YAML rules against regulations that amend without notice, with their own roadmap conceding that change detection is not built yet - so the first failure mode is a document auto-approved against a superseded rule, reported with a citation that still resolves to a real but obsolete clause. Second: the escalation threshold, since auto-approve on 'routine' documents is only as safe as the classifier that calls a document routine.

what_it_does.value: Upload a document (PDF, text, CSV or image). An ingestion agent extracts the facts with Gemini; a compliance agent reasons over them against the ruleset for that industry and jurisdiction and returns a risk score where every verdict carries its citation. Routine documents auto-approve, edge cases escalate to a human reviewer with the reasoning attached, every decision is appended to an immutable audit trail, and a scheduled workflow produces weekly reports with a Gemini executive summary. Currently 16 rulesets, 88 rules, 12 jurisdiction profiles: NDIS and aged care in Australia, corporate compliance in India, and GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, LGPD, PDPA and POPIA.

what_it_is.value: Document compliance checks where every verdict must cite a rule in a versioned ruleset, with an append-only audit trail the writing identity cannot rewrite.

what_to_steal.value: Grant the writer identity the append permission and deny it the job-starting permission, so history cannot be rewritten by the application that writes it; derive tenant identity only from verified token claims so there is no request field to tamper with; record prompt and model version against every generated verdict so a decision can be reproduced months later; make environment variables required rather than defaulted, because a permissive default on a fresh checkout silently removed credentials.

hazard.note: Compliance verdicts on NDIS, aged-care and privacy obligations, with routine documents auto-approved. The page argues its case for trustworthiness at length - citations, versioning, immutability - but does not state who is accountable when an auto-approved document later becomes an audit finding, nor whether the rulesets were reviewed by a practitioner.

complianceguardian-kcqs32.worth_note: The product decision is the transferable one: refuse to let a model answer unless the answer names a rule from a versioned file, and escalate when it cannot. Pair that with an audit trail enforced at the permission layer and an entitlement model that spends counters inside a transaction, and you have three moves that apply to any agent product expected to produce evidence a third party will rely on. The incident write-up is unusually useful too - six failures behind each other, none of which crashed.

built_with_verified.value: declared by the authors (7): express-on-firebase-app-hosting-(cloud-run-under-the-hood), firebase, firestore, firestore-for-persistence, react, typescript, vite · no repository published, so these are the team's own claim and nothing corroborates them

clone_cost.note: our estimate with assumptions visible; not a claim about the team

assumptions: grounding you can pin per region: search access to each region's press, plus a stated fallback label for when a region returns nothing
a citation pipeline that canonicalises publisher URLs, since redirect-chained citations are the part agents will inherit broken
editorial capacity for the synthesis and the corrections page, which the product presents as human curation and cannot automate without contradicting itself
a QA pass on what a lens may assert beyond its sources, before anyone treats the Claim objects as evidence rather than as framing
value.estimate: 6-9 weeks for the agent roster plus the schema surface; another quarter for the four media pipelines and the editorial tooling
value.why: The core loop is a fan-out with grounding: one event, N lens prompts each pinned to a region's outlets through search grounding, rendered side by side with tone labels - a few weeks in React, Express and Firestore, and the SPA-plus-Cloud-Run shape is well trodden. The work that is not routine is the surface the page treats as the product: emitting valid Claim-partitioned structured data per perspective with citation arrays, resolving grounded URLs to canonical publisher addresses (its own open defect), and keeping a public llms.txt, OpenAPI document and no-auth endpoint honest as the schema evolves. The radio bulletin, song and portrait video are each a separate third-party integration that fails silently often enough that the author wrote it up. And the editorial layer - curating Common Ground, maintaining /corrections - is recurring human cost rather than build cost, which is why a clone of this is smaller than its feature list and bigger than its line count.

data_and_models.value: Gemini 3 Flash with Google Search grounding runs every lens, pointed at each region's own outlets; Gemini Native Audio renders the daily radio bulletin; Imagen 4 makes the topic imagery; Suno makes the per-topic songs; Firestore persists topics, perspectives and donor records, and Firebase Storage holds media. No model is trained and no retrieval configuration is published: the page states no per-region coverage figure, no rate at which a lens's sentences are unsupported by the cited source, and no fallback policy for when a region's press is unreachable - while naming that exact failure as the thing that turns multi-perspective AI into ventriloquism. The measured numbers on the page are about the surface (schema score, load time), not about the journalism.

how_it_works.value: React 19 with TypeScript and Vite as a client-side SPA, Express on Firebase App Hosting (Cloud Run underneath), Firestore for persistence and Firebase Storage for media, Imagen 4 for imagery and Gemini 3 Flash with Search grounding for the lens agents. The part the page spends most of its technical detail on is the machine-readable surface: every topic page ships a schema.org NewsArticle whose hasPart is an ItemList of Claim items, each with a per-perspective @id anchor and its own citation array, and the Jester carries a disambiguatingDescription marking it as satire so downstream models will not read it as fact. Alongside it: llms.txt and a 42,000-word llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document, IndexNow pings, and a fully public no-auth /api/topics/recent endpoint.

how_they_tested.value: No evaluation of journalistic quality is described: no precision or recall against a labelled set of regional articles, no inter-rater check between lenses and human correspondents, no measurement of how often a perspective's claim is unsupported by its own citation, and no test-suite mention. The closest thing to a measurement on the page is an unnamed 'recent independent GEO audit' that scored schema 99/100 and Trustworthiness 82/100 - a machine-readability audit of metadata, not of content accuracy, with no auditor, date or rubric published. The one figure that does carry a before/after denominator is load time (30-45s to under 1s TTI), and the page volunteers a measured defect count in the same area: about ninety unresolved grounding redirect URLs per topic page.

limits_they_disclosed.value: The challenges section is a set of post-mortems rather than a list of feature difficulty. Firebase App Hosting silently ignored the hosting block in firebase.json, so sitemap and RSS returned 404 with no error anywhere, and the fix was explicit Express proxies in server.ts. Suno failed quietly: a null data payload produced an undefined taskId, JSON.stringify dropped the key, and the client polled /api/music/status/undefined fifty times against {code: 200, data: null}; it was fixed at three layers - a real 502 from the server, bailing after five consecutive nulls, and refusing to start on an empty, 'undefined' or 'null' id. On iOS Safari under ITP and some carriers, an App Check ReCaptcha V3 token was the reason for a 30-45 second blank splash. And a Firestore rule written for /donations/{docId} did not match the client's /donors/{docId} path, which went unnoticed for months because the Admin SDK bypasses rules - so only the admin UI was broken, silently.

value.relation: both convert an unverifiable judgement into a machine-checkable artifact - a signed finding in a CI matrix against a Claim object with a citation array - and both leave the same gap: the artifact proves the format, not the accuracy of what is inside it. ACM measures its own detectors while Newspectives does not measure its lenses, which is the sharper omission given that the lens output is read as fact by other models.

both attach citations to language a model generated and both keep a human as the writer of record, but they differ on direction and schedule: Continuity re-checks existing claims over time and hands back a diff, Newspectives generates fresh accounts of one event across regions and hands back a comparison. Neither publishes a false-negative rate, and in both cases that rate is what the user is actually buying.

both sit in the sector where the hazard question is sign-off and both answer it with transparency rather than authority - methodology, editorial-standards and corrections pages against an audit-ready rule set. The pair is the catalog's clearest illustration that disclosure and compliance are different objects: one tells a reader how the output was made, the other tells an auditor what was checked.

what_breaks_first.value: The grounding fallback. When a region's outlets are unreachable - a paywall, a regional block, a story too new to have local coverage - the lens still produces fluent text, which is the exact failure the page names as ventriloquism, and there is no published policy for it and no rate for how often it happens. Second, citation integrity: about ninety redirect URLs per topic page still resolve through Vertex rather than to the publisher, so the citation array an agent inherits is a chain of third-party hops that can rot or 404 independently of the article. Third, the Jester: satire is marked with disambiguatingDescription, which most consumers ignore, so a joke line becomes a Claim in someone else's context window. Fourth, the Common Ground synthesis - labelled editorial curation on the site, but a downstream reader who takes the ItemList and drops the framing gets a machine-generated consensus view of a contested event, which is the one artifact this product's own principles say not to produce.

what_it_does.value: For a news event, roughly twenty configured regional lenses (about thirteen enabled by default - USA, China, Russia, India, Germany, UK, Israel, Arab World, Latin America, South Africa, a Humanitarian lens, a satirical 'Jester' and a Common Ground synthesis) each produce an account of the same story, grounded with Google Search against that region's press - BBC, Global Times, RT, Al Jazeera, NDTV, Times of Israel are the outlets named. The output is presented side by side with a tone classification and citations per perspective, and the Common Ground panel is an editor-curated synthesis rather than a model verdict. Three adjacent formats ride the same pipeline: a daily eight-minute AI radio bulletin on Gemini Native Audio, a per-topic Suno song, and a 20-second portrait video. Transparency pages are part of the product rather than a footer - /methodology, /editorial-standards and /corrections name the model and admit its limits.

what_it_is.value: A roster of about thirteen regional-lens agents reads one news event against each region's own press and publishes the frames side by side as schema.org Claim objects with citations - so the machines downstream inherit the framing, not just a flattened headline.

what_to_steal.value: Ship claim-level structured data rather than page-level: NewsArticle to hasPart to an ItemList of Claim objects, each perspective with its own @id anchor and citation array, so a consuming agent can attribute a sentence to a lens instead of to a URL. Use disambiguatingDescription to mark non-factual voices inside the same structure, and publish llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, an OpenAPI document, IndexNow pings and an unauthenticated read endpoint - treat machine readers as an audience and the transparency pages become distribution. Then take the operational post-mortems, the most reusable content on the page: never return a 200 with a null payload (make it a real 502), bail after five consecutive nulls instead of polling an 'undefined' id fifty times, refuse to start on an empty or 'undefined' config value, treat silently ignored hosting config as untrustworthy and proxy it explicitly, dismiss splash screens in about 150ms and load auth and settings in the background, and remember that Admin SDK paths bypass security rules, so rule-only tests prove nothing about an admin UI. Last: keep synthesis human and say so on the page.

newspectives-new-perspective-on-news.name: Newspectives - new perspective on news
verdict_reasons: soundness 0.59 over 64% of the rubric; 0 named unknown(s) remain → publishable with caveats
newspectives-new-perspective-on-news.worth_note: The wedge is different in the way that matters for an agent-read catalog: it treats other models as first-class readers of a news product and builds for them - NewsArticle objects whose hasPart is an ItemList of Claim objects, one per perspective, each with its own anchor and citation array, a disambiguatingDescription marking the satirical lens so it is not quoted as fact, llms.txt, a 42,000-word llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, OpenAPI, IndexNow pings and an unauthenticated recent-topics endpoint. Almost nobody has taken that position, and for a product whose output will be summarized by machines it is the correct one: an agent should inherit the framing and the citations rather than a flattened paragraph. The editorial judgement is as sound as the plumbing - side by side rather than a merged balanced answer, Common Ground labelled as human curation, transparency pages at /methodology, /editorial-standards and /corrections. What holds it short of breakthrough is that the hard part is not built here: grounding quality, which the page itself names as the whole difference between perspective and ventriloquism, is unmeasured, and roughly ninety unresolved citation redirect URLs per topic page says the last mile of the citation layer is still open.
